questions.question: If cars are passing you on both sides while you drive in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: Drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than traffic, use the right lane.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you are far enough ahead. When you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to move back.

questions.question: What should you do when passing on a two-lane road?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Oncoming vehicles may look slower than they really are. Always make sure you can safely change lanes. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you pass.

questions.question: How can you help the driver behind you stay at a safe distance?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Drive at a steady speed and signal your turns, lane changes, and slowing down in advance. This helps other drivers maintain a safe distance.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.
Checking your rearview mirrors regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors regularly.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every two to five seconds. Staring straight ahead is dangerous. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beam headlights.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Slow down and use low beam lights in fog. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait.

questions.question: Traffic on the freeway is merging into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to keep your spot.
Always stay in your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When traffic allows, make room so vehicles can merge safely into your lane.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: How can you avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Braking while in a curve may cause you to skid.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping so other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians know your plans.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in work zones?

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not tailgate and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance.

questions.question: What is the proper way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner in the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal before you turn. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb when approaching the intersection.

questions.question: As your speed increases, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your stopping distance increases with speed. At high speeds, look far ahead so you have time to react to hazards safely.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a curved ramp that goes downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before a curve. You may not see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve can cause a skid.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed carefully.
Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Slowly pass vehicles that appear to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At intersections and crossings, look left and right to see if anyone is coming into your path.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right then sharply left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop before crossing the intersection.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for traffic, and go carefully.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what lights should you use?

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Use your parking lights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What happens if you brake hard continuously on ice and snow?

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, causing you to lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, causing you to lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice locks the front wheels and causes you to lose steering. Slow down to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning in rainy weather?

options.text: Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down in rain to prevent hydroplaning. When you drive too fast, your tires ride on water and lose contact with the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: A school bus ahead has flashing red lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have exited.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. Exception: You do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Be ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending. Be ready to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil and dirt on the road that has not washed away yet. Drive carefully during the first half hour of rain.

questions.question: On a slippery road, what following distance should you maintain?

options.text: No different than normal.
Farther from the car ahead than normal.
Closer to the car ahead than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther from the car ahead than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road. Keep a longer following distance when the road is slippery.

questions.question: When should you yield your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
questions.explanation: Always yield if it prevents a collision. Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way.

questions.question: On a one-way street, when can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: If you increase your speed before the turn.
If traffic on that street moves to the right.
If traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street only if traffic moves to the left, unless a sign prohibits it. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: Why is winter driving more dangerous?

options.text: Ice, snow, fog, and freezing temperatures make roads unsafe.
There are more hours of darkness.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Winter creates many hazards: fog, rain, snow, sleet, ice, and more darkness. Prepare for these conditions when driving in winter.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are prohibited.
You may proceed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road, entrance, or exit. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around.

questions.question: Can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.
Yes, if there are two or more lanes in your direction.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What problems can strong wind gusts cause on highways?

options.text: They affect only large vehicles.
They only reduce visibility.
They can affect all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can affect all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, not just large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility and can physically move your vehicle.
